claim: A resource endpoint lets you privately access a VPC resource, such as a database in another VPC, and resource endpoints don't require a load balancer; without resource endpoints you had to add an internet gateway or use an interface endpoint with a Network Load Balancer. The PrivateLink document history dates this to December 1, 2024.

evidence.quote: Without resource endpoints, you have to either add an internet gateway to your VPC or access the resource using a AWS PrivateLink interface endpoint and a Network Load Balancer.

A resource endpoint lets you privately and securely access VPC resources such as a database, an Amazon EC2 instance, an application endpoint, a domain-name target, or an IP address that may be in a private subnet in another VPC or in an on premise environment.
Resource endpoints don't require a [load balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glossary/latest/reference/glos-chap.html#loadbalancer), so you can access the VPC resource directly.

| [Access resources and service networks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/privatelink-access-resources.html) | AWS PrivateLink supports accessing resources and service networks across VPC and account boundaries. | December 1, 2024 |
